about.title: About Yivi
about.slogan: With Yivi, you are in control.
about.who_is_behind_Yivi_item: Who is behind the Yivi app?
about.who_is_behind_Yivi_explanation:
Yivi is made by the **Privacy by Design** foundation.  This foundation emerged in 2016 from the Digital Security research group at Radboud University in Nijmegen. The foundation is independent and non-profit.

The Yivi app is developed as open source in collaboration with SIDN, the registry of the .nl domain. Development also involves cooperation with various government bodies and with the healthcare sector. Around 30 municipalities are involved, including Nijmegen, Amsterdam and Leiden. Yivi won the Dutch Privacy Awards 2018.
about.why_Yivi_explanation:
**Yivi exists because you have the right to an online identity that truly belongs to you.** Yivi is not a commercial app used to track you, profile you and sell your personal data to third parties.

Yivi is designed in the spirit of the [General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0040940/2019-02-19). With the Yivi app, you only show those details about yourself that are relevant and necessary in a given situation.

**With the Yivi app, you keep your identity in your own hands, in the secure Yivi app on your own mobile.** The Yivi app is a powerful tool for identifying yourself (online) and for signing digitally. With respect for your privacy.
about.privacy_explanation:
The Yivi app is built so that you, and only you, can see and use your personal data in the app. Your personal data is stored only on your mobile and not somewhere in the cloud.

The Yivi app is built so that a website or shop where you identify yourself can (cryptographically) verify that the data you show is genuine.

The Yivi app shows your data directly from your mobile to a website. Nobody else can see that you are identifying yourself there. Not even the organisation behind Yivi can look along. 

By using Yivi you agree to the privacy policy [link].
about.responsibility_explanation:
The website that offers a Yivi login asks for the data needed to log in. In the Yivi app, you decide whether to agree to share the requested data.
Does a website ask for too much data? Then it is wise not to agree. You can also consider filing a complaint. You do that with the website itself or with the [Dutch Data Protection Authority](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/nl/zelf-doen/gebruik-uw-privacyrechten/klacht-melden-bij-de-ap).

With the Yivi app you can also place a digital signature. Such a signature can have (legal) consequences. So think carefully before you place a signature with the Yivi app.

When you place a signature with the Yivi app, you acknowledge that the Privacy by Design foundation is in no way a party to any agreement you enter into via a Yivi signature. The foundation is not responsible or liable.

manual.faq_info: How do you use Yivi? See the explanation below.
manual.question_1: How can I log in to a mobile website with Yivi?

answer_1.step_1: Open the website on your mobile and choose to log in with Yivi.
answer_1.step_2:
The Yivi app starts automatically.
Enter your PIN.
answer_1.step_3: Give permission (or not) to share your data.
answer_1.step_4:
After sharing, you are logged in.
You can now use the website.

manual.question_2: How can I log in to a website on my computer with Yivi?

answer_2.step_1: Open the website on your computer and choose to log in with Yivi.
answer_2.step_2: Open the Yivi app on your mobile and enter your PIN.
answer_2.step_3: Start the QR code scanner in the Yivi app. Scan the QR code on your computer screen.
answer_2.step_4: Give permission (or not) to share your data.
answer_2.step_5:
After sharing, you are logged in.
From now on you can use the website.

help.title: Help
help.faq_info: See whether your question is listed here.
help.question_1: What can I do with Yivi?
help.answer_1:
With Yivi you can easily log in and identify yourself. You only show the details about yourself that are needed. For example, to watch a certain film, you prove that you are over 16, and nothing more. You can also sign documents digitally with Yivi. You only use relevant attributes of yourself, in a kind of digital stamp. This way you can sign with Yivi as a doctor, as a citizen or in another role.

More and more websites let you log in with Yivi. Doctors, for example, can use Yivi to access medical records on the website [helder](https://www.helder.health/). Especially municipalities and the healthcare sector are now working on further use of Yivi so that you can log in there with Yivi. To get an impression of the possibilities, you can try out a number of Yivi [demos](https://privacybydesign.foundation/demo/) yourself.
help.question_2: What do I do if I lose my mobile?
help.answer_2:
If you lose your mobile, nobody can get into your Yivi app, provided you chose a good PIN.

You can protect yourself even better: when installing Yivi you were given the option to provide an email address. If you did, you can block the use of your Yivi app via [MyYivi](https://privacybydesign.foundation/mijnYivi/). Then absolutely nothing can happen with the Yivi app on your old, lost mobile.

If you have not yet added an email address in [MyYivi](https://privacybydesign.foundation/mijnYivi/), you can still do so. It is wise to do that now.

On your new mobile you can reinstall the Yivi app and fill it again with your data. After that you can simply carry on.
help.question_3: What makes Yivi privacy-friendly and secure?
help.answer_3:
Your personal data is protected with your PIN. Your data is stored in the Yivi app on your mobile and not in the cloud.

In the Yivi app, your personal data has been digitally signed by the source (issuer) the data comes from (for example the national government or the municipality).

As a result, when you identify yourself, a website or shop can cryptographically verify that the data is genuine. 
This exchange of personal data takes place directly between your mobile and that website. Nobody else can see that you are identifying yourself there. Not even the organisation behind Yivi can look along.
help.question_4: Where is my Yivi data stored?
help.answer_4:
Your data is stored in the Yivi app on your mobile and *not* in the cloud.

You always give explicit permission (or not) yourself to pass your personal data from the Yivi app to a website.
If you delete your data from the Yivi app, it is really gone from Yivi.
help.question_5: Why is data in the Yivi app only valid for a limited time?
help.answer_5:
In Yivi you can see on each card how long it is valid. That validity period depends on the type of data and how changeable it is. Your name and date of birth are valid for five years, but your address only for one year. The source (issuer) of the data determines the validity period. So the validity of data can expire. The Yivi app warns you about this.

You can always refresh your data, even without a warning, by retrieving it again from the source. For example, after your 18th birthday you can retrieve your data from your municipality again and use the Yivi app to prove that you are over 18.
help.question_6: Can I put Yivi on a second mobile or tablet?
help.answer_6: Yes, on every device (Android or iOS) you can open a separate Yivi account and fill it with cards containing your data. It is wise to do so. If you lose one device, you can still log in with the other device.
